messages:
maria: Night shift handoff — quick notes before I head out. Main things: 1) Small latency bump on `model-serve-3` around 03:10 UTC (p95 ~420ms -> 580ms), started after the autoscaler bump. Was transient but kept an eye on it. 2) KV cache hit-rate on `dedicated-pool-a` dropped to 62% for ~15m, likely due to a newer routing rule; I reverted rule and hit-rate recovered. 3) Canary deploy of quantized rtx-7 model is running (canary=10%), no errors so far.
jon: Thanks Maria. For the latency bump — any correlating infra events? nodes restarting, OOMs? logs?
maria: No OOMs. No pod restarts. Looking at CPU steal on the host (small spike). No disk IO issues. Suggest watching: p95 latency, cpu_steal, and `grpc_retries` metric. I added those to the oncall dashboard under "night-watch".
sam: Pinged oncall dashboard, saw the cpu_steal spike at 03:09. Could be noisy co-tenancy on the dedicated pool. Recommend enabling `sched_isolate` on the problematic hosts if it recurs. I'll open infra task if we see it 2x in 24h.
kevin: @maria @sam noted. Also FYI — I left a small config change in `routing/rule-7` to prefer lower-latency replicas. Reverted after you flagged kv drop. I put a comment in the PR: https://git.internal/repo/PR/3421
maria: Thanks. Action items: sam to monitor hosts and open infra task if cpu_steal repeats; kevin to add canary rollback monitor (I added a synthetic check for canary error-rate); alana to take first watch for next 4h.
alana: Taking first watch. Quick ask: where's the canary rollback playbook? I couldn't find it in docs.
maria: It's under runbooks/canary-rollback.md — shortcut: `/docs canary-rollback` in Confluence. TL;DR: scale canary to 0, route traffic to model-serve-2, and run validation set. If in doubt ping me or @jon.
deploy-bot: [deploy] canary-deploy/model-rtx-7 started by kevin at 03:28 UTC — canary=10%.
jon: Small reminder: if you see sustained p99 > 1s for >5 minutes, follow post-deploy rollback steps. Also, if KV hit-rate stays <70% for >10m, run `scripts/flush_cache.sh --pool=dedicated-pool-a` and monitor warmup. Info in runbook.
alana: Noted. I'll watch p95/p99, kv hit-rate, and canary error-rate. If anything pops I'll call handoff.
oncall-bot: Scheduled handoff reminder — @maria handing off to @alana at 04:00 UTC.
maria: Extra FYI: there's an ongoing code-review for `batching/tight-merge` that touches the batching scheduler. If it lands during your watch it might affect throughput briefly. PR: https://git.internal/repo/PR/3450 — @sam please ping reviewers if it needs fast review.
sam: Will do. I'll also throttle any merges that look like they'll spike mem usage. If you want to pre-approve I can queue.
kevin: One minor ops note — the billing alert threshold for dedicated-pool-a was relaxed last week. If you get a billing spike alert, that's probably a false positive until finance adjusts threshold next month. I'll follow up.
maria: OK thanks. Final checklist for @alana: (1) watch p95/p99 latency for model-serve-3, (2) watch kv cache hit-rate for dedicated-pool-a, (3) monitor canary error-rate and synthetic check, (4) be ready to run `scripts/flush_cache.sh` or scale canary down. Escalation: ping @jon then paging policy if no reply in 10m.
alana: Got it. Taking over — I'll post another update in ~2h or on any notable changes. :thumbsup:
